scope: Black-source-face-control retakes for six human-residual windows in the 660-frame flower film
summary: All six source-face-suppressed A800 retakes produced human-free raw Wan candidates, but none is authorized for stitching until named flowers, two independent hands, contact, and temporal gates pass.
evidence: Physical A800 GPUs 2, 3, 4, and 5 generated starts 0, 72, 326, 470, 542, and 571 with seed 42, relighting LoRA routing, and an exact black source-face control.
Every raw wan_output.mp4 decodes 88 frames at 896x512 and 30 FPS; the immutable run manifest preserves all six candidates.
Every-fourth-frame review of all six raw candidates finds a closed robot face panel and no source-human face, skin, sleeve, or torso.

Postprocessed candidates at starts 0, 72, and 542 contain only 70 frames at 24 FPS; starts 326, 470, and 571 contain 88 frames at 30 FPS, so downstream work must use and deterministically retime the raw Wan output.
The generated flowers visibly differ from the real source instances, so human removal alone is insufficient for acceptance.
lessons: Suppressing source-face identity control generalizes the anchor's complete-human-removal behavior across difficult poses.
The proxy's postprocessing can truncate an 88-frame raw candidate to 70 frames; raw Wan preservation is required before timeline correction and instance restoration.
limitations: Dense review is an internal Codex semantic audit, not independent human annotation.
No retake in this batch has passed source-to-candidate flower identity, two-hand, contact, or temporal acceptance.
next_actions: Retime each raw Wan output to the exact 89-frame, 24-FPS source timeline.
Restore source-tracked named flowers, track both robot hands independently, and run the unchanged strict object/contact gate per window before overlap stitching.
